name: Christian Light Math
line: Christian Light Math is a low-cost print course the adult teaches and grades. AMP checks and explains every answer.
description: AMP vs Christian Light Math: a low-cost print course the adult teaches and grades, or practice that places, checks and reviews by itself. Prices and evidence.
verdict: Christian Light Math is a low-cost print course for grades 1 through 12 from a nonprofit Christian publisher, with continuous review in its lessons and fact drills in the early grades [2][3][4][5]. The adult teaches from the guide and checks the work against the answers [10]. AMP finds the level in each part of math, checks and explains every answer as it is given, and times review to each learner.

reasons.title: Each answer explained before the next problem
reasons.body: In Christian Light Math the answers are in the Teacher's Guide or an answer key, and the adult checks the work against them [10]. The Answer Key Sets list answers without a full solution for every problem; full solutions come with the textbook courses' solution keys [5]. AMP marks each answer as it is given and shows the correct answer and the worked steps before the next problem. The learner sees why while the problem is still in front of them.

reasons.title: Less teaching and grading for the adult
reasons.body: Christian Light's Teacher's Guide gives the adult detailed teaching instructions and the answers [10]. The younger grades add oral and flash-card drills, and the grade 7 textbook option is described as requiring more teacher involvement [2][6]. AMP brings a one-step hint and a written lesson with a worked example to every problem type, plus narrated films for a growing share of them. The adult has nothing to plan, teach or grade.

reasons.title: A level in each strand, not one course
reasons.body: Christian Light places a learner in one course with a diagnostic test, and recommends beginning that test at least one grade below the child's grade [8][11]. From there the learner works the course's lessons in a fixed order; the grade 5 and grade 7 sets run to 170 lessons [5][6]. AMP places the learner within the first 24 problems and keeps a level in each of 14 strands of math and keeps adjusting. A child who is ahead in measurement and behind in fractions practices each where it stands.

reasons.title: Gaps send practice back to the prerequisite
reasons.body: Quizzes and tests are built into the 170 lessons of the grade 5 set [5]. We found no mastery rule stated in the pages we read, so how to use the scores, and when to go back to earlier work, is not set out there. In AMP, two misses or helped answers in a row on a skill send practice to what that skill builds on. A skill counts as Strong only when four of the last five answers are right without help.

reasons.title: Review timed to each learner, not to the page
reasons.body: Christian Light builds review into its daily lessons, and many exercises return to earlier work [4][10]. That is a real design. The research we draw on points further: mixed, spaced practice beat blocked practice, 62% to 38% on the researchers' own test a month later, in a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders [15]. AMP sets the timing for each learner and each skill: 6 hours, 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and a month, mixed with other topics. A miss starts that skill's schedule over.

reasons.title: Paper made for one learner
reasons.body: Every Christian Light student in a grade works the same printed LightUnits [2]. AMP prints unlimited workbooks built from the learner's own record: a warm-up, today's idea, practice, the review that is due and a challenge, each with a worked answer key. Results entered from paper count toward the learner's level. A family that wants pencil and paper keeps it.

rows.price: Grade 5: $55.50 for the year's ten LightUnits and $31.90 for the Teacher's Guide set, bought once [5]. Algebra 1 LightUnits are also $55.50 [7].
rows.buyers: Families, Christian schools and churches, through its online store [1][8].
rows.range: Grades 1-12: Math 1-8, Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2, then Functions and Trigonometry [2][9].
rows.start: A diagnostic test places the learner in a course. The publisher recommends beginning the test at least one grade below [8][11].
rows.teaching: Printed lessons in a workbook, taught by the adult from a Teacher's Guide [10]. Algebra 1 has optional instructor videos on USB [2][7].
rows.next: The next lesson in a fixed order: ten LightUnits a year, 170 lessons in the grade 5 set, quizzes and tests included [2][5].
rows.mastery: Quizzes and tests inside the lessons [5]. No mastery rule found in the pages we read.
rows.review: Earlier work is reviewed in the daily lessons [4][10]. No schedule for when a skill returns found in the pages we read.
rows.print: Print is the course: workbooks, textbooks, guides, answer keys and flash cards, the same for every learner [2][5].
rows.adult: Teach each lesson from the guide, run oral and flash-card drills in younger grades, and check work against the answers [2][10].
rows.reports: A paper report card for LightUnit scores, behavior and attendance; the monthly progress report is a PDF download [8].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found. No entry in Evidence for ESSA and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report [13][14].

theirs: Christian Light Math comes from Christian Light Publications, a nonprofit publisher in Harrisonburg, Virginia, founded in 1969 [3]. It serves homeschools, Christian schools and churches [1]. The math line runs from Math 1 through Math 8, then Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2, and Functions and Trigonometry [2]. Geometry and Functions and Trigonometry are based on Alpha Omega Publications courses [2].

A year of math is ten LightUnits: consumable workbooks. The grade 5 and grade 7 sets hold 170 lessons, quizzes and tests included [5][6]. Each daily lesson brings in new ideas gradually, and many exercises review earlier work [10]. The younger grades add oral and flash-card speed drills [2]. Grades 4 through 8 can also be bought as a textbook [2]; the grade 7 listing says that option requires more teacher involvement [6].

The adult teaches from a Teacher's Guide with detailed teaching instructions and the answers, and checks the work [10]. Placement is by a diagnostic test [11]. Algebra 1 adds optional teaching videos on a USB drive, in which an instructor introduces and demonstrates each lesson's concept [7].
credit: Price. A year of grade 5 math is $55.50 for the workbooks and $31.90 for the Teacher's Guide set, bought once [5]. AMP costs far more.

Fact drills in the early grades: oral and flash-card speed drills, multiplication tables 0 through 10 memorized by the end of Math 3, and photocopiable drill sheets [2][12]. The What Works Clearinghouse practice guide for elementary students who struggle in math lists regular timed activities to build fluency among six recommendations, each rated strong evidence [17]. AMP has no timed drills.
Paper-based, with no internet needed for the workbooks and guides [2]. AMP needs a connection to practice, though its workbooks print.

A full grades 1 to 12 math line from a Christian publisher, plus what it calls "an accredited recordkeeping and diploma program for homeschool families" [1][2][8]. AMP offers no accreditation, transcript or diploma.
An instructor on video for Algebra 1, for families who want a person to explain each lesson [7]. AMP's films are animated, with synthesized voices.

theirs: We found no outcome study of Christian Light Math on the pages of its site we read, in Evidence for ESSA or in the What Works Clearinghouse's list of intervention reports, as of November 2026. It has no entry in Evidence for ESSA and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report [13][14]. The site pages we read describe the curriculum in general terms and cite no study [1][8].

Its claims are modest. Course pages say new ideas are taught through incremental learning and continuous review, and the Algebra 1 page says the course "takes the fear and misunderstandings out of the equation" [10][7]. Neither page cites a study.
ours: Two of AMP's rules take on work a print course leaves to the adult, and both draw on published research. Feedback that explains: across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in all ages and subjects, it averaged an effect of 0.49, against 0.32 for the correct answer alone and 0.05 for right or wrong only [16]. Review spread out and mixed with other topics beat blocked practice in a randomized trial that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations [15]. AMP gives explained feedback at every answer and schedules review. We expect that to show in outcomes, and we have committed to measuring it in public.

AMP is new, and its own outcome studies have not run yet. They begin in 2027: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. Until then, the research behind each part of AMP is laid out in our report, and the code is public.

them: Choose Christian Light Math if price comes first: a year of grade 5 math is under $90 in workbooks and guide.
Choose Christian Light Math if you want math on paper, with no screen at all.
Choose Christian Light Math if you want daily speed drills and flash cards for math facts.
Choose Christian Light Math if you want a Christian publisher's grades 1 to 12 line and a diploma program it describes as accredited.
amp: You would rather not teach and grade every math lesson yourself.
Your child is ahead in some parts of math and behind in others.
You want every answer checked and explained the moment it is given.
You like the LightUnits and want practice beside them that finds the gaps and schedules review.
You want to try before paying: 100 answers and 5 workbooks free, with no card.

questions.question: Is AMP more expensive than Christian Light Math?
questions.answer: Yes, by a wide margin. A year of Christian Light grade 5 math is $55.50 for the LightUnits plus $31.90 for the Teacher's Guide set, bought once [5]. AMP is $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child and $399 or $39 for each more; that buys placement in every strand, a chosen and checked problem every time, scheduled review and unlimited personalized workbooks from counting through precalculus.

questions.question: Can we use AMP alongside Christian Light Math?
questions.answer: Yes. A family can keep the LightUnits for daily lessons and use AMP for checked practice and review. AMP places the learner within the first 24 problems and keeps a level in each strand, so it does not need to know which LightUnit your child is on.

questions.question: Does AMP have speed drills like Christian Light?
questions.answer: No. AMP has fact-practice problems but no timed drills. Christian Light builds speed drills and flash cards into its early grades and sells photocopiable drill sheets [2][12].

questions.question: Has Christian Light Math been shown to work in studies?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study. It has no entry in Evidence for ESSA and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report as of November 2026 [13][14].

questions.question: Is AMP accredited like Christian Light Academy?
questions.answer: No. AMP gives report cards and progress reports, but no transcript, credit or diploma. Christian Light offers Christian Light Academy, a recordkeeping and diploma program it describes as accredited [8].
